To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) nearinfrared diffuse optical tomography (DOT) can detect early changes in tumor oxygenation in breast cancers during NAC, which correlate with pCR, and (2) DOT can detect early changes (within 2 wk) in tumor metabolism in breast cancers duringNAC, which correlate well with pCR.

1) near-infrared diffuse optical imaging can be used to measure the response of breast cancers to neoadjuvant therapy and that 2) the response of breast tumors can be predicted using the changes in the optical signal measured by the device.
NIR-DI and 18F- FDG PET/CT can both be used to predict pCR after NAC for breast cancer, with similar accuracy, but that NIR-DI is more accurate than 18F-F DG PET/CT at predicting non-pCR.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a novel optical imaging technique for the early prediction of response to NAC.
the development and validation of an imaging-based prognostic model for breast cancer response to NAC.
the development of an optical imaging system for breast cancer detection and characterization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of PET in the evaluation of patients undergoing neoadjuvant therapy for breast cancer is of limited utility.
the current data do not support the use of 18F-FDGPET/CT for the early prediction of breast cancer response to neoadjuvant chemotherapies.
the current data do not support a routine role for PET imaging in the assessment of response to NAC in breast cancer patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the combination of NIR-DIO and 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (18F-FDG) PET/CT can provide complementary information in the prediction of pCR to NAC in breast cancer, with NIR-DIO being the more sensitive technique for the early detection of response.
the near-infrared (NIR) imaging system has the potential to be an important imaging modality in the clinical setting.
we have demonstrated that the near-infrared (NIR) diffuse optical (DO) imaging system, which is a noninvasive optical imaging system, can provide an accurate assessment of the tumor response to NAC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NIRDI can be a useful tool for monitoring breast cancer response to neoadjuvant treatment.
near-infrared diffuse optical imaging (NIDOI) can provide a noninvasive, quantitative, and objective measure of breast cancer response to NAC.

near-infrared (NIR) diffuse optical imaging can be used to predict pCR to NAC in breast cancer patients, with a specificity and sensitivity of 100% and 85.7%, respectively, in a pilot study of 7 patients.
